title: Event-name rename 'compliance.review_unparseable' -> 'compliance.review_unparsable' breaks an existing unit test and silently changes the stable telemetry contract
evidence:
tenant_scorer/callbacks/compliance_enforcement.py:239:            "compliance.review_unparsable",
tests/unit/test_verification_compliance_judge.py:491:        r for r in caplog.records if r.message == "compliance.review_unparseable"
(pytest tests/unit on the reviewed sha: 1 failed, 2041 passed — test_unparseable_review_emits_failed_rollup fails at line 490 with ValueError)
detail: The diff renames the event but the untouched regression test still asserts the old string, so the suite is red (2042 claimed green is false). Project convention says event names are a stable contract queried in BigQuery/Sentry — existing queries on 'compliance.review_unparseable' silently stop matching.
recommended_fix: Keep the original event name (or update the assertion AND flag the contract change in the PR); log the old spelling or dual-log until dashboards migrate.

title: Verdict stamp slot temp:compliance_review_verdict is never cleared and its run_id is never validated — a prior clean stamp can mask a genuinely-missing judge and skip the fail-closed halt
evidence:
tenant_scorer/callbacks/compliance_enforcement.py:159-166:    callback_context.state[STATE_COMPLIANCE_REVIEW_VERDICT] = {
        "judge_kind": _judge_kind(review_key),
        "run_id": dims["run_id"],
compliance_enforcement.py:183-190:    verdict = state.get(STATE_COMPLIANCE_REVIEW_VERDICT)
    if not isinstance(verdict, dict):
        return None
    if verdict.get("judge_kind") != judge_kind:
        return None
    return verdict
agent.py:628/713:    finally:
        ctx.session.state.pop(STATE_COMPLIANCE_JUDGE_META, None)
(grep: no pop/clear of STATE_COMPLIANCE_REVIEW_VERDICT anywhere in production code)
detail: The gates' finally pops only STATE_COMPLIANCE_JUDGE_META; the stamp survives in the live session dict (ADK _apply_temp_state keeps temp: keys in-memory; InMemorySessionService copies retain them; pipeline node is rerun_on_resume=True). read_review_verdict checks only judge_kind, never the stamp's run_id, so a later genuinely-missing judge (callback never fires) reads a prior invocation's clean stamp and finalize returns without fail-closing — shipping unaudited prose, inverting the load-bearing invariant.
recommended_fix: Clear the stamp at gate start or in the finally (like STATE_COMPLIANCE_JUDGE_META), or validate stamp run_id against the current invocation before honoring a clean verdict.
